Creating a reproducible, blinded randomisation list

Source: vignettes/randolist.Rmd
randolist.Rmd

This guide shows how to make a randomisation list with randolist, following the OUCRU SOP PR-BST-DM-001 Creating Randomisation Lists (v008). The package is a revision of the legacy createRandoListNew.R: for the same seed and settings it gives the same list, so existing studies can switch without their lists changing.

library(randolist)

Who does what

The SOP keeps the trial statistician blinded by splitting the work:

Step Who What
4.1.b Statistician (RA) Writes the code and makes a dummy list (seed known, arms named *_Dummy).
4.1.c Head of Biostatistics Reviews and approves the code.
4.1.e–f Pharmacist Sets the dummy flag to FALSE, replaces the seed with a new random seed, runs the code.
4.1.g Pharmacist Checks the final list (e.g. balance within blocks) and stores it in the secure Pharmacy folder.

Only the seed and the dummy flag differ between the dummy and the final code. Everything below is designed so that this switch cannot go wrong silently.

1. The statistician’s dummy code

Put these settings at the very top of the study script. DUMMY controls the arm names and the output file names; check_final_setup() stops the final run if the seed was not changed.

DUMMY      <- TRUE        # pharmacist: set to FALSE
DUMMY_SEED <- 20261104    # seed of the dummy list (known to the statistician)
SEED       <- DUMMY_SEED  # pharmacist: replace with generate_seed() output

check_final_setup(dummy = DUMMY, seed = SEED, dummy_seed = DUMMY_SEED)
#> DUMMY list: arm names get the suffix '_Dummy'. The pharmacist must set DUMMY <- FALSE and replace the seed for the final list.
arm_names <- dummy_arm_names(c("Dex", "Pla"), dummy = DUMMY)
arm_names
#> [1] "Dex_Dummy" "Pla_Dummy"

Now generate the list. Use the SOP block lengths explicitly (4 and 6 with probabilities 0.75 and 0.25 for two arms) and make the list at least twice as long as the largest anticipated stratum.

rl <- createRandoList(
  nPat             = 200,          # 100 anticipated patients x 2
  arms             = 2,
  arm_names        = arm_names,
  strata           = c(HTD = "001"),
  blocklength      = c(4, 6),
  blocklength_prob = c(0.75, 0.25),
  seed             = SEED
)
head(rl, 8)
#>   pat_id stratum_name stratum block_number       arm   RanNo
#> 1    001          HTD     001            1 Dex_Dummy 001-001
#> 2    002          HTD     001            1 Pla_Dummy 001-002
#> 3    003          HTD     001            1 Pla_Dummy 001-003
#> 4    004          HTD     001            1 Pla_Dummy 001-004
#> 5    005          HTD     001            1 Dex_Dummy 001-005
#> 6    006          HTD     001            1 Dex_Dummy 001-006
#> 7    007          HTD     001            2 Dex_Dummy 001-007
#> 8    008          HTD     001            2 Pla_Dummy 001-008

Passing seed inside the call is the same as calling set.seed(SEED) just before it, but makes it impossible to forget. The function also remembers how the list was made:

str(attr(rl, "rando_info")[c("seed", "rng_kind", "R_version", "blocklength_prob")])
#> List of 4
#>  $ seed            : num 20261104
#>  $ rng_kind        : chr [1:3] "Mersenne-Twister" "Inversion" "Rounding"
#>  $ R_version       : chr "R version 4.6.2 (2026-10-29)"
#>  $ blocklength_prob: num [1:2] 0.75 0.25

2. Check the list

check_rando_list() confirms that randomisation numbers are unique and that every complete block is balanced. The last block may be incomplete because the list is cut at nPat.

check_rando_list(rl)
#> Randomisation list check: OK
#> 
#>  stratum   n                         arms n_blocks block_sizes
#>      HTD 200 Dex_Dummy=100; Pla_Dummy=100       44  4x32; 6x11
#>  complete_blocks_balanced last_block_balanced
#>                      TRUE                TRUE

3. Write it with SOP file names

write_rando_list() builds the file name from the study, the dummy flag, the MonthYear and the R version (SOP 4.1.b), and writes a log with the MD5 sum of each file and the session information.

out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "24EI_Nov2026")   # in practice: the study subfolder
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
files <- write_rando_list(rl, dir = out_dir, study = "24EI", dummy = DUMMY,
                          overwrite = TRUE)
basename(files$file)
#> [1] "24EI_dummy_Nov2026_R4.6.2.csv"     "24EI_dummy_Nov2026_R4.6.2_log.txt"

It refuses combinations that would break blinding:

# arm names say "Dummy" but the flag says final
write_rando_list(rl, dir = out_dir, study = "24EI", dummy = FALSE)
#> Error:
#> ! dummy = FALSE but arm names contain 'Dummy'. Set the dummy flag consistently.

# a final list may not go to a Biostatistics folder
biostat <- file.path(tempdir(), "BIOSTATISTICS")
dir.create(biostat, showWarnings = FALSE)
final_like <- createRandoList(20, arm_names = c("Dex", "Pla"), seed = 583920175)
write_rando_list(final_like, dir = biostat, study = "24EI", dummy = FALSE)
#> Error:
#> ! A FINAL list must not be written to '/tmp/Rtmp0eqmi4/BIOSTATISTICS' (matches forbidden_dirs). Write it to the secure Pharmacy folder.

4. What the pharmacist changes

The pharmacist receives the approved script and changes only the three lines at the top (and the output folder):

DUMMY      <- FALSE
DUMMY_SEED <- 20261104          # leave as is
SEED       <- 583920175         # from generate_seed(), not a memorable number
out_dir    <- "<secure Pharmacy folder>"

Get the new seed once with:

generate_seed()
#> [1] 930683011

Then run the script in a clean session so no copy of the list is left in a workspace file: Rscript --vanilla 24EI_randolist.R. If the seed was not changed, the script stops:

check_final_setup(dummy = FALSE, seed = 20261104, dummy_seed = 20261104)
#> Error:
#> ! FINAL list requested but the seed is still the dummy seed. Replace it with a new random seed (see generate_seed()).

Keep the final code, CSV, log and PDF together in the Pharmacy folder. The log contains the seed, so it must not be copied to the Biostatistics folder. When making the PDF for pharmacy procedures, leave out the block_number and permute.block columns: they reveal the block structure.

A template script with all of this is installed with the package:

file.copy(system.file("templates", "rando_list_template.R", package = "randolist"),
          "24EI_randolist.R")

Stratified randomisation

Combine strata with composite_strata(). Each stratum gets its own blocks; the stratum code is part of the randomisation number.

strata <- composite_strata(site = c(HCMC = "1", HN = "2"),
                           age  = c(Child = "C", Adult = "A"))
strata
#> HCMC.Child   HN.Child HCMC.Adult   HN.Adult 
#>      "1-C"      "2-C"      "1-A"      "2-A"

srl <- createRandoList(nPat = c(60, 40, 80, 40), strata = strata,
                       arm_names = arm_names, blocklength = c(4, 6),
                       blocklength_prob = c(0.75, 0.25), seed = SEED)
names(srl)
#> [1] "HCMC.Child" "HN.Child"   "HCMC.Adult" "HN.Adult"
head(srl$HCMC.Child, 4)
#>   pat_id.stratum stratum_name stratum block_number       arm  RanNo
#> 1             01   HCMC.Child     1-C            1 Dex_Dummy 1-C-01
#> 2             02   HCMC.Child     1-C            1 Pla_Dummy 1-C-02
#> 3             03   HCMC.Child     1-C            1 Pla_Dummy 1-C-03
#> 4             04   HCMC.Child     1-C            1 Pla_Dummy 1-C-04

By default the strata are generated one after another from a single random stream (as in the legacy code), so changing the size of one stratum changes the strata after it. If a stratum may need to be extended later, use seed_per_stratum = TRUE: stratum i then uses seed SEED + i - 1 and the strata no longer depend on each other.

a <- createRandoList(c(20, 30), strata = c(A = "1", B = "2"), seed = SEED,
                     seed_per_stratum = TRUE, patid_format = list(width = 3, flag = "0"))
b <- createRandoList(c(50, 30), strata = c(A = "1", B = "2"), seed = SEED,
                     seed_per_stratum = TRUE, patid_format = list(width = 3, flag = "0"))
identical(a$B, b$B)
#> [1] TRUE

Permuting patient numbers

n.block_permute shuffles the patient numbers within every n blocks, so the numbers on the packs do not follow the allocation order. Be clear about which order patients are enrolled in:

  • if patients receive the next row of the list, balance holds at the end of every block, as usual;
  • if patients receive the next randomisation number, the shuffled numbers define the sequence and balance is only guaranteed at the end of each group of n.block_permute blocks (with Inf, only at the end of the stratum).
p <- createRandoList(24, arm_names = arm_names, blocklength = 4,
                     n.block_permute = 2, seed = SEED)
p[, c("pat_id", "block_number", "permute.block", "arm", "RanNo")]
#>    pat_id block_number permute.block       arm  RanNo
#> 1      07            1             1 Pla_Dummy 001-07
#> 2      06            1             1 Pla_Dummy 001-06
#> 3      03            1             1 Dex_Dummy 001-03
#> 4      04            1             1 Dex_Dummy 001-04
#> 5      02            2             1 Pla_Dummy 001-02
#> 6      01            2             1 Dex_Dummy 001-01
#> 7      05            2             1 Pla_Dummy 001-05
#> 8      08            2             1 Dex_Dummy 001-08
#> 9      16            3             2 Dex_Dummy 001-16
#> 10     11            3             2 Pla_Dummy 001-11
#> 11     12            3             2 Dex_Dummy 001-12
#> 12     14            3             2 Pla_Dummy 001-14
#> 13     10            4             2 Pla_Dummy 001-10
#> 14     15            4             2 Pla_Dummy 001-15
#> 15     13            4             2 Dex_Dummy 001-13
#> 16     09            4             2 Dex_Dummy 001-09
#> 17     17            5             3 Dex_Dummy 001-17
#> 18     23            5             3 Pla_Dummy 001-23
#> 19     24            5             3 Dex_Dummy 001-24
#> 20     20            5             3 Pla_Dummy 001-20
#> 21     22            6             3 Pla_Dummy 001-22
#> 22     21            6             3 Dex_Dummy 001-21
#> 23     18            6             3 Pla_Dummy 001-18
#> 24     19            6             3 Dex_Dummy 001-19

Reproducibility checklist

  • Copy the package version (or the function file) used into the study folder; the log records randolist and R versions.
  • Set the seed in the call (seed =) and keep sample_kind the same for the dummy and the final list. The default "Rounding" matches the legacy code; "Rejection" is R’s current default and equally reproducible.
  • Re-running the final code must give the same MD5 sum as in the log.
  • The function restores your random number settings when it finishes, so code that runs after it is not affected.

Differences from the legacy createRandoListNew.R

Same seed + same arguments give the same list, with these exceptions, which are all deliberate:

  • Two bug fixes, both only when patient numbers are permuted (n.block_permute > 0):
    • the legacy code could give a wrong or duplicated patient number when the last permutation group held a single patient (sample(41, 1) samples from 1:41). The new code keeps the correct number; all other rows and the following strata are unchanged;
    • when all permutation groups had the same size, the legacy code stopped with “pat_id not found”. The new code works.
  • Lists whose randomisation numbers would not be unique are refused.
  • Strata with fewer patients than arms (or none) are allowed.
  • The caller’s sample.kind is restored instead of being reset to "default".

The package tests run the legacy file side by side with the new code over many seeds and settings to confirm this. The article Where the legacy code goes wrong shows every case with runnable code.
